content: After adjusting for the effect of anisotropy, on average, less than 5% of the variance in a word's contextualized representations can be explained by their first principal component. This holds across all layers of all models. This suggests that contextualized representations do not correspond to a finite number of word-sense representations, and even in the best possible scenario, static embeddings would be a poor replacement for contextualized ones. Still, static embeddings created by taking the first principal component of a word's contextualized representations outperform GloVe and FastText embeddings on many word vector benchmarks.
